Right, listen carefully, because this is the part people get wrong every single year. The project is done in groups of four and it is marked in two separate ways. Half of the mark is given to the group, for the final presentation, and half is given to you individually, for your section and for how you worked in the team. That second half is decided by two things: my notes, and the peer review form that is filled in by the other three people in your group. So no, you cannot disappear for three weeks and turn up on presentation day. Drafts are collected on the fifteenth and the final version is due on the twenty-ninth. Everything is submitted through the portal, and everything is checked for plagiarism automatically.

Hey, it's Owen, from the group. So I looked at the rubric properly and we have been doing this wrong. The biggest section is not the content, it is the analysis, which is worth forty percent on its own. We have written a lot of facts and almost no argument. Also the presentation has to be twelve minutes, not twenty, and marks are taken off if you go over. I've put the slides in the shared folder. Could you take the second part, the comparison? Your section was the clearest one in the draft, honestly, and mine was described by the teacher as, and I quote, a list. Anyway, let me know if you want to swap.

The teacher hands out the rubric and explains how the project is marked. The group meets at lunch and each person is given one section. Lais writes the comparison and sends it to the shared folder. The drafts are collected on the fifteenth and comments come back a week later. On the last day the presentation is delivered and the peer review forms are filled in.
